sections.h2: Where is Alexandria, VA, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Alexandria is an independent city on the west bank of the Potomac River, about 15.35 square miles in size, with Washington, D.C. to the northeast, Arlington County to the north and northwest, and Fairfax County to the south (Wikipedia). Elevation runs from sea level to 287 feet.

Because it is an independent city, Alexandria bills its own real estate tax and has no county government above it. The city's main neighborhoods give a sense of the housing mix:

  • Old Town, the historic core near the river
  • Del Ray and Potomac, the former town of Potomac
  • Carlyle and Eisenhower East
  • Rosemont, West End, Potomac Yard and Arlandria

The city had 159,467 residents in the 2020 census and a 2025 estimate of 160,662. Median household income was $124,593 in the 2024 American Community Survey estimate.

sections.h2: What is the history that still shapes Alexandria property?
sections.html:
Alexandria was founded in 1749, became a town in 1779 and was ceded to the District of Columbia in 1801 before returning to Virginia in 1847. It was chartered as a city in 1852 and became independent in 1870, and annexations in 1915, 1930 and 1952 expanded its borders.

The Old Town historic district, created in 1946, was the third in the country. That history is why many Alexandria houses are regulated by a review board, as the next section explains.

sections.h2: Do historic district rules affect selling an Alexandria house?
sections.html:
They can, because exterior work in a local historic district needs approval from the Board of Architectural Review. The city regulates two local districts, Old and Historic Alexandria and Parker-Gray, plus buildings designated as One Hundred-Year-Old Buildings (Historic Preservation page).

  • A Certificate of Appropriateness is required for new construction and exterior alterations visible from a public right of way.
  • A Permit to Demolish is needed to demolish or encapsulate more than 25 square feet of material, whether or not it is visible.
  • Interior work does not need board approval.
  • Staff can approve some projects administratively, usually in under five business days.

The city offers a Historic Preservation map viewer to check whether an address is in a district. Preservation staff can be reached at 703.746.3833 or Preservation@alexandriava.gov.

The federal government is the largest force in the city's economy. The biggest employers named are the Pentagon's Mark Center, with about 8,000 workers, and the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office, with about 6,000. Tourism passed $1 billion in visitor revenue in 2024.

Metro's Blue and Yellow lines serve the city, with stations at King Street-Old Town, Braddock Road, Eisenhower Avenue and Van Dorn Street, and a Potomac Yard station that opened in 2023. The city runs its own DASH bus system, and Interstates 95, 495 and 395 and US 1 pass through it.

Alexandria City Public Schools operates 12 elementary schools, two pre-K through 8 schools, two middle schools and Alexandria City High School, which has two campuses.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 Alexandria assessment show?
sections.html:
Alexandria's total tax base rose 3.41 percent for 2026, the fifteenth straight year of net increase, and residential assessments rose 4.40 percent overall. The figures come from the Office of Real Estate Assessments notice insert (2026 key dates insert).

Category2026 figure
Average existing residential value$757,706 (up 3.81%)
Average single-family home$1,045,750 (up 4.44%)
Average condo$460,185 (up 2.81%)
Commercial overallup 1.91%
Officedown 3.40%

Of residential properties, 63 percent went up, 8 percent went down and 29 percent stayed the same. Only sales completed before January 1, 2026 counted toward the assessed values.

sections.h2: What are the 2026 Alexandria tax dates in order?
sections.html:
The city's 2026 key-dates insert lists the full calendar, and the notice itself is not a bill. The calendar below uses the dates printed on that insert.

  • February 25: assessment notices mailed.
  • March 16: deadline to request an administrative review. The city says no exceptions will be made to appeal deadlines.
  • April 15: deadline for elderly and disabled tax relief applications.
  • April 29: City Council adopts the FY 2027 budget and sets the tax rate.
  • June 1: deadline to appeal to the Board of Equalization.
  • June 15: first-half payment due, even if a review or appeal is pending.
  • Early October: second-half bills mailed.
  • November 16: second-half payment due. November 15 falls on a Sunday in 2026.

To start a review, email realestate@alexandriava.gov or call 703.746.4168.

sections.h2: Does Alexandria offer tax relief for older or disabled owners?
sections.html:
Yes. Alexandria runs a real estate tax relief and deferral program for owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled. Completed applications or annual certifications are due to the Department of Finance by April 15 each year (program page).

  • Household net assets may not exceed $430,000, excluding the home, up to one acre of land and the related mortgage.
  • Household gross income counts the applicant, a spouse and other owners living in the home.
  • Late applications may be accepted until April 15 of the next year for good cause, such as a hospitalization or first-time filing.
  • Deferred taxes are repaid with interest when the property is conveyed or the owner dies. Relieved taxes are not repaid.

The city's phone line is 703.746.4800, option 6, and the email is taxrelief@alexandriava.gov. The page we opened did not show the income limit, so ask the office for the current figure.

The deferral matters in a sale. If you deferred tax, the repayment falls due when the house is conveyed, so ask for the balance at the start.

sections.h2: Does the Potomac flood Old Town properties?
sections.html:
Parts of Old Town flood during storm surge and some low inlets flood from the tide alone. A city analysis of Potomac gauge data from 2004 to 2021 found the river above Action Stage about 112 days a year and above Flood Stage about 16 days a year (city flood frequency memo).

EventRiver level
Hurricane Isabel, September 20038.66 feet, highest on record
Great Potomac Flood, March 19367.40 feet
October 2021 nor'easter5.99 feet
Tropical Storm Ernesto, September 20065.54 feet

The memo names King Street at Strand and Union, and Union Street from Prince to Thompsons Alley, among the areas that flooded in 2021. Anyone selling near the waterfront should expect buyers to ask about flood insurance and past water in the basement or garage.

sections.h2: What does a deed transfer cost in Alexandria?
sections.html:
Virginia's state recordation tax on a deed is 25 cents per $100, applied to the greater of the price or the most recent assessment (Va. Code 58.1-801). A separate grantor's tax is 50 cents per $500 (58.1-802), and it excludes the value of liens that stay on the property.

The title company will prepare a settlement statement that shows these charges and the property tax payoff. Local and other recording charges are not covered here, so ask the title company.

sections.h2: How do sellers with Alexandria tax due usually proceed?
sections.html:
An Alexandria seller with unpaid tax can sell, and the title company pays the balance from proceeds. Ask the Treasury Division for a payoff that includes any penalty, and confirm whether the half-year bill already issued has been paid.

This page is general information. The city offices and a Virginia attorney can confirm figures for your parcel.

faqs.q: When is Alexandria property tax due in 2026?
faqs.a: The first half is due June 15, 2026, and the second half is due November 16, 2026, because November 15 falls on a Sunday. The city says the first payment is due even if a review or appeal is pending.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Alexandria assessment?
faqs.a: Request an administrative review by March 16, 2026, then appeal to the Board of Equalization by June 1 if you still disagree. Email realestate@alexandriava.gov or call 703.746.4168.

faqs.q: Does Alexandria have tax relief for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, can apply by April 15 each year, with household net assets capped at $430,000 excluding the home and up to one acre. Call 703.746.4800, option 6.

faqs.q: Do I need approval to change the outside of a house in Old Town?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if the house is in a local historic district and the work is visible from a public right of way. The Board of Architectural Review issues a Certificate of Appropriateness, and interior work does not need it.

faqs.q: How much did Alexandria assessments rise in 2026?
faqs.a: The total tax base rose 3.41 percent and residential assessments rose 4.40 percent. The average single-family home was valued at $1,045,750 and the average condo at $460,185.
